title: Where Lester's improvising came from: marches
summary: Phillips says nobody out there was playing what Lester wanted to hear; his improvising came from inside and began on marches like Shouting Liza.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: What to think while improvising: wrong notes and being in the moment

blocks.x: Do you know anybody that he would have listened to besides...? Were there any records he was into?
Well, there wasn't many cats out there
playin' nothin' in them days. You didn't have nothin' to listen to. They wasn't playin' nothin' he wanted to hear, because he was playin' more than they was playin'.
Where did he actually get the idea to improvise?

Well, he just started off that way. He played a march that way. Like, we used to play "Shouting Liza". You never played that. That's a march. [SINGS ARRANGEMENT UP TO LESTER YOUNG's SOLO AND THEN THE FIRST FEW BARS] That's when the old man said he was going to take him off the alto and put him on the tenor! Ha!
So he was already playing on the marches in 1924, then.
Sure! On the end of the trios, it's a pell mell at the end... Shit, man, he'd tear them up.
So he was already into that by the time you knew him. And that's the way he learned? Is that what you understood? The way he learned to improvise is by playing on marches?
Well, he learned... It was just within him to do that. Yeah, that's what it was; just him that played that way. Because anything he played, he improvised.
Anything that he played, he gonna put something' to it and make it sound. He gonna dress it up, I'd say that. Yeah, he'd dress it up. Anything that he played, he would dress it up.
